previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and hypogammaglobulinemia was admitted for evaluation of chest pressure, shortness of breath, and dizziness after developing symptoms while running errands in the heat. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was ruled out by normal EKG and negative cardiac enzymes. His symptoms were attributed to dehydration, supported by elevated creatinine and BUN, with improvement following IV fluid rehydration. He also received a scheduled IVIG infusion without adverse reaction, using a different manufacturer and premedication to prevent prior issues. An abdominal X-ray showed nonspecific bowel gas pattern with no obstruction, and he remained stable throughout the admission. All home medications were continued without change. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to maintain hydration, complete outpatient GI follow-up with a second KUB, and continue baseline therapies.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
